links.outcome: Simulated clinician burden of disagreement-guided presentation pipeline versus baseline all-findings display
links.effect: With disagreement model TPR 0.8, FPR 0.03 and 5% second-read probability, burden reduced by 4.8% ± 0.2%; burden rose 12.04% at FPR 0.10. Automation-bias protection itself not measured.
links.quote: Combining all of these, if the disagreement model TPRs and FPRs are 0.8 and 0.03, respectively, and the conditional probability of a second read is 0.05, burden is reduced by 4.8% ± 0.2%.

links.outcome: Burden impact of deferring/second-read requests on predicted disagreement findings
links.effect: Even if all clinically significant disagreements receive a second read, burden increases only 6.67% ± 0.07%; restricting to under 5% reduces burden by 4.8% ± 0.1%.
links.quote: Even if all cases of disagreement on clinically significant findings receive a second read, burden is only increased by 6.67% ± 0.07%.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of clinician burden to disagreement-model false positive rate (operating point)
links.effect: An FPR of 0.01 gives 9.55% ± 0.06% burden reduction, whereas an FPR of 0.10 gives a 12.04% ± 0.09% increase.
links.quote: Although an FPR of 0.01 can result in an expected 9.55% ± 0.06% reduction in burden, an FPR of 0.10 actually results in a 12.04% ± 0.09% increase.

links.outcome: Rate of radiologist-AI disagreement in deployed chest X-ray tool
links.effect: Average disagreement rate 6.5% (median 2.6%); prevalence-weighted TPR 76.4% and FPR 4.1% versus final report. Automation bias not directly measured.
links.quote: The average and median rates of disagreement between the final radiologist label and the diagnostic model label for the Nam Dinh Hospital sample (independent of the predicted ROIs) were 6.5% and 2.6%, respectively (IQR, 1.3–9.6).
